results.title: Classic Barbecue Sauce
results.description: Nothing more American (besides Apple Pie and Jazz) than a good barbecue sauce. Thick, savory, tangy, with a touch a sweet. As you can probably tell we love barbecue sauce. Unfortunately that touch of sweet has transformed into hammer of sweet with many commercial barbecue sauces. Here at Hangry Herbivore treat sugar as another seasoning. The secret to a good sauce is the molasses and Smokey seasoning. Trust us, don’t sub it for anything else. Use blackstrap molasses for the extra nutrients. Coconut sugar has a lower glycemic index, meaning it should spike blood sugar less. However feel free to use any sugar if coconut sugar is not available. One last thing; take the time to simmer the sauce. Your friends, family, and taste buds will be humming happy, soulful songs of thanks. Please do enjoy and stay tuned for more.

instructions.text: Mix all ingredients into a medium sized pot
Whisk bowl until all ingredients are incorporated and a smooth, uniform sauce is formed.
Simmer pot over medium heat for 15- 20 minutes. This will enhance the flavor of the sauce. Skip if you need to but you won’t want too.
Allow sauce to cool and transfer to a jar. We love using mason jars for our sauce.
This barbecue sauce can be used immediately while warm or stored in a refrigerator for later use.

results.title: Garlic Sesame Beans
results.description: Want a quick simple dish with loads of flavor? We got you covered. These green beans hit the salty and savory notes really well. This recipe was inspired by a cooking class we took. And we are proud to pass it on to all of you. Please do enjoy!

instructions.text: Fill stock pot with water and bring pot to boil

If you have raw sesame seeds. Heat a cast iron skillet over medium high heat. Once skillet is hot(not smoking), place seeds in and toast until golden brown. Don’t over toast though or the seeds will be bitter.
Heat frying pan over medium heat.
Mince garlic.
Place beans in blanching basket and cook for 20-40 seconds. The beans should retain a bright green color.
Drain beans and add to frying pan. Add garlic, sesame seeds, and seasonings.
Cook for 1 - 2 minutes.
Serve hot and enjoy

results.title: Beer Bread
results.description: What’s not to love about beer bread?It’s moist, dense, slightly sweet, and delicious. And best of all, it’s cheap and fast to make. We learned about beer bread many years ago at the 99 cent only store. They sold Larry the Cable Guy branded beer bread. We bought it and we were sold. It became our go to for potlucks, cookouts and family events. Try this with a Pilsner or lager. The cheaper the better. The beer provides carbonation for making the bread rise. For a really rich flavor try an IPA or a stout (Old Rasputin…). As with any baking, all purpose flour will make for more pillowy goodness. Whole wheat flour has more nutrients but makes the bread more dense. Going half works well to. Have fun experimenting this one.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
Sift flour into mixing bowl.
Add baking powder, salt, and sugar to mixing bowl. Stir until dry mixture looks uniform.
Pour the can of beer into the bowl. Mix until a batter is formed. It should be somewhat thick. Make sure all of the dry ingredients are incorporated.
Grease loaf pan with the oil.
Pour batter into the loaf pan.
Put butter on top of the batter in the loaf pan.
Place loaf pan in the oven and bake for 60 minutes.
After baking, allow bread to cool for 10 minutes before cutting and serving.

results.title: Barbecue Tofu Nibs
results.description: This one is a family delicacy. Here's the thing: vegans like barbecue too. The smokey flavor and wonderful barbecue sauce. Enter tofu, our perfect meat sub. It absorbs sauce and flavor just like a sponge. And unlike your over used kitchen sponge you'll want to eat these delicious nibs when they are done. We like the super firm high protein variety because it is very easy to use right out of the package. No pressing necessary. But regular firm tofu will also work. Just make sure to press it using a good tofu press to remove excess water. Too much water and it will puddle in the air fryer( or oven). Lastly, make a homemade sauce. Like this one. You'll love it even more. Enjoy!

instructions.text: Cut tofu into cubes
Place tofu into an air frier.
Coat tofu in the avocado oil
Set air frier to 400 degrees F  and cook for 10 minutes. Stir tofu after 5 minutes have passed
Pour in barbecue sauce. Use enough to generously coat the tofu.
Cook for another 5 minutes in the air frier at 400 degrees F.

results.title: Rustic Almond Flour Cake
results.description: Want to have your cake and eat it too? Stay tuned for this incredible almond flour cake. We swapped most of the all purpose flour for almond flour. Almond flour is made of ... almonds. They are a decent source of protein, dietary fiber, riboflavin, vitamin E, manganese, magnesium, copper and phosphorus, and monounsaturated fats. That's a lot of nutrients for a dessert. Are we trying to advertise cake as a health food? Of course not! But hey, if you're gonna have cake, why not have it made of almonds (mostly). This cake will have a rich dense texture. Think pound cake not angel's food cake. Top it off with a nice glaze for extra sweet but it isn't really needed. Although this is a dessert, you could prepare it the night before and have it for breakfast the next morning. Hope you enjoy this indulgent but healthy treat.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F
Grease 8 or 9 inch cake pan with butter.
Add all other ingredients to stand mixer bowl. Use whisk attachment
Whisk until a batter is formed and be careful not to over mix.
Transfer batter to cake pan and bake for 25 minutes.
Allow cake to cool for 10 minutes and remove carefully from pan.
Transfer to cooling rack. Cool for another 10 minutes.
Ice cake or enjoy sans icing.

results.title: Cashew Cheese Spread
results.description: Every refrigerator needs a few good spreads. With a good spread you can make an easy sandwich, a fancy dip for veggies or just for snaking out of a jar. Enter our cashew cheese spread. You’ll want to have this one hand. It’s been a staple for years and a real party favorite. We use raw cashews but roasted cashews will the spread a toasted flavor. The balsamic vinegar gives the spread a sweet tanginess. The smoked paprika and liquid smoke combo brings the smoke. And who can say no to nutritional yeast. This Smokey, tangy, and creamy spread will become a tradition in your family too.

instructions.text: Soak cashews in water for 12 hours or overnight.
Place all ingredients in a blender and blend until cashew cheese has a smooth consistently. Use more water for a thinner cheese.
Serve and enjoy.

results.title: Tofu Scramble
results.description: There is an endless amount of vegan egg products on the market. From vegan powder egg substitute for baking to faux hard boiled eggs. It is really great these products exist but they can be pricey. There is one that has been with us the whole time. That’s right, the great tofu scramble. When mashed and fried it does more than replace scrambled eggs. It becomes a dish with its own identity and infinite flavoring opportunities. We’ll discuss some of those here. Back during our days as omnivores, we would elevate scrambled eggs with fresh herbs like marjoram or oregano from our potted garden. Add some to your scramble. You get some from your neighborhood community garden or the grocery store. Dried herbs can work too; just don’t keep them for more than 6 months. Now tofu naturally lacks the liquid of an egg yoke. Thats where the sunflower or cashew crema comes in. It will add the liquid and creamy fat to your tofu scramble. It thickens when heated so you want it to have a higher water content. That’s our secret. Now you know too. Speaking of water content,  e sure to press your tofu. Especially true if you are not using super firm high protein tofu. Please do enjoy making this for your family and friends.

instructions.text: Coat cast iron skillet or frying pan with oil. Heat pan over medium heat
Sauté onion for about 2 minutes, until the onions are translucent.
Stir the crumbled tofu into the pan. You can use a potato masher to break apart the tofu or just use your hands. Sauté for three minutes.
Add the garlic, bell peppers, and seasonings to the pan and sauté for another minute.
While the tofu is cooking put the water and cashews or sunflower seeds into a blender and blender into smooth.
Pour crema into the pan. Add nutritional yeast if you are using.

Add a capful of liquid smoke. It will be tempting to add a lot more because it smells like bottled firewood(we always are). But liquid smoke is a very strong ingredient; too much will over-power the dish.
Cook until crema has started to thicken. Stir occasionally.
Serve finished dish with toast and jam, fruit or anything you like.

results.title: Vegan Box Cake
results.description:
Love cake but don't have time make bake from scratch? After reading this you will see the bakery isle as a friend and helper. Before we continue, let's just say that baking from scratch is always going to be better. You have control over all the ingredients. But that is more time. You can buy a little help from your grocery store and still make a wonderful vegan cake. It will be egg free, dairy free, moist and delicious. Here's what you need: Box cake mix, soy milk (or any plant based milk), oil, and plant based yogurt. Most box mixes require milk, oil, and eggs. Most oil is already vegan. We like soy milk for baking for the protein content and relatively neutral flavor. For eggs, you can use plant yogurt instead. The yogurt adds nice texture to the cake, keeping it moist and smooth. Sometimes necessity brings good ideas. One year for our daughter's birthday we decided to buy a birthday cake. It was during the pandemic where everyone was opening their own personal bakeries. So, we found a baker who made vegan cakes. We paid and were eagerly awaiting the birthday party and the scrumptious cake that was sure to be there. One problem; on pickup day one day before the party our would-be neighborhood baker ghosted us. No answer from the phone. And the address was a random apartment building. We were PO'd for sure. But there was no time for time. We had a party with little munchkins who would be anticipating a cake. That's how our little hack was born. The icing part was even easier. Many store-bought icings are already vegan. 

We have since used this recipe hack for two birthday parties and everyone asks where we purchased that cake from. And there were never any leftovers. The whole party was buzzing from the flavorful cake with a little sugar high thrown in there ;). Try it for your next event or for your next dessert at home.

instructions.text: Preheat Oven (follow instructions on box). It will most likely be 350 degrees F.
Grease Pan with Oil
Add all ingredients to a stand mixer bowl or any bowl
Mix all ingredients together until a consistent batter is formed.
Pour batter into pan and bake according to instructions on the box.
Wait 20 minutes before icing. Serve with vegan ice cream or just by itself.

results.title: Vegan Biscuits
results.description:
Close your eyes. Imagine something freshly baked, warm from the oven — buttery, fluffy, golden at the edges like your favorite cloud. Now open them, because that's exactly what you're about to make.
Just 5 simple, inexpensive ingredients and a little patience. Let's get into it.
Choosing your flour — you've got options here, and they all behave a little differently. All-purpose gives you that classic smooth, tender crumb. Whole wheat brings more fiber, nutrients, and a heartier flavour, but a slightly denser texture. Almond flour is smooth with a subtle nuttiness, though it's the densest of the three. You can also mix and match — white whole wheat sits right between all-purpose and regular whole wheat and is a great middle ground. For this recipe we use a combination of all-purpose and white whole wheat.
We love coconut cream here — it gives the biscuits a rich, luscious creaminess. Full-fat coconut milk works as a swap if that's what you have on hand.
One important note: don't skip preheating, and don't be put off by the high temperature. That heat is what gives these biscuits their rise and golden top. Trust the process.
Eat them warm with butter and jam, slathered in your favorite nut butter, or built into a sandwich. However you serve them, we have a feeling they won't last long.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 450 degrees Fahrenheit
Combine all ingredients in a large bowl using a wooden spoon.
Mix until a wet dough is formed.
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Use an ice cream scooper to scoop a dough ball and place onto the lined pan.
Bake for 8-10 minutes.
Serve with warm butter and jam.
